name: GrapheekDB
tagline: Small pure-Python embedded graph database with pluggable LMDB or Kyoto Cabinet storage; unmaintained.
description: GrapheekDB is a lightweight graph database written in pure Python by Raphaël Braud. It stores directed graphs of nodes and edges with arbitrary properties and offers a Gremlin-inspired, chainable traversal API with property indexes. Storage is pluggable: an in-memory backend for tests, or Kyoto Cabinet and LMDB key-value stores for persistence, and it could also run as a small server. Releases ran from 0.0.1 in January 2014 to 0.0.25 in October 2020, all still labelled pre-1.0, and the project has seen no activity since. Python developers who want an embedded graph today usually choose LadybugDB (the Kùzu fork), CozoDB or NetworkX on top of SQLite.
statusNote: No releases since 0.0.25 (October 2020); the Bitbucket project is inactive.
strengths: Pure Python with no server to run
Pluggable LMDB or Kyoto Cabinet persistence
Chainable traversal API familiar to Gremlin users
weaknesses: Pure-Python traversals are slow on large graphs
GPL v3 limits embedding in proprietary software
useCases: Small embedded graph prototypes in Python
Learning how a graph layer maps onto a key-value store
